findings.title: Cooperative close requires no payee consent, so the payer can close at a stale cumulative amount and refund themselves unpaid service
findings.exploit: Both signatures checked by close() come from the payer side: `signature` from channel.authorizedSigner (the payer or the payer's delegate, set by the payer in openChannel) and `payerSignature` from channel.payer. The payee signs nothing and msg.sender is unchecked. The payer consumes service and hands the payee vouchers up to cumulative X, which the payee has not yet settled on-chain (the documented flow settles later). The payer then signs a fresh voucher with cumulativeAmount = channel.settled (or any value below X) plus a matching CLOSE message and calls close(). The grace period is bypassed, the channel is finalized, the payee receives cumulativeAmount - settled (zero), and the payer is refunded deposit - cumulativeAmount. The payee's outstanding vouchers can no longer be settled because settle() reverts on a finalized channel.
findings.impact: Payees lose every unsettled voucher on every channel; the payer receives service for free. This defeats the payment channel's core guarantee.
findings.fix: Require the payee's authorisation for an immediate close (payee signature over channelId and cumulativeAmount, or msg.sender == payee), or make close() only accept a cumulativeAmount greater than or equal to the highest voucher by routing through the grace-period path.

findings.title: authorizedSigner of address(0) lets any invalid signature settle the full deposit
findings.exploit: openChannel() never rejects authorizedSigner == address(0) (lines 221-252). _recoverSigner returns address(0) for a signature of the wrong length (line 188-190) and raw ecrecover also returns address(0) for an invalid signature. On such a channel, settle() compares the recovered address(0) with channel.authorizedSigner (address(0)) at line 317 and passes. Anyone submits a voucher with cumulativeAmount = deposit, an increasing nonce, a future expiry and an empty signature, and the entire deposit is transferred to the payee.
findings.impact: The payer's entire deposit on any channel opened with a zero signer (a natural 'default to payer' client value) can be settled to the payee without any service being delivered; a malicious payee drains it directly.
findings.fix: Revert in openChannel when authorizedSigner is address(0) (or default it to msg.sender), and in _recoverSigner revert instead of returning address(0); prefer OpenZeppelin ECDSA.recover, which also rejects malleable signatures.

findings.title: Anyone can start closure, and finalize can be sniped at grace-period end before the payee settles
findings.exploit: initiateClose() has no caller check, so any address can start the one-hour close on any channel, and the grace period can never be extended or reset. finalize() is also callable by anyone. The payer, having consumed service against vouchers the payee intends to settle later, calls initiateClose() and then calls finalize() in the first block at or after gracePeriodEnd. If the payee has not submitted its latest voucher within that hour (or is front-run in the final block), the channel finalizes and the payer receives deposit - settled; later settle() calls revert with ChannelAlreadyFinalized.
findings.impact: Payees lose unsettled earnings whenever they do not react within a fixed one-hour window that anyone can start without notice.
findings.fix: Restrict initiateClose to the payer or payee, let finalize be called only by the payee during a window after grace end (or let settle extend gracePeriodEnd), and size the grace period to realistic payee settlement latency.
